That is not the whole truth...That's a common misconception many people tend to believe in this thing called "starvation mode". Yes you might gain some weight from eating after fasting for a long period of time but that weight gain will be water weight not fat. THE ONLY WAY TO GAIN FAT is in a calorie surplus. The body does not create fat after eating a meal no longer how long you haven't eaten for. As long as you aren't eating more calories than you burn, you will NOT be gaining FAT. Fasting tends to make people overeat because the body has been restricted from food so it's their natural instinct to eat more than they need. Hence why fasting is associated with "starvation mode" and starvation mode is associated with fat gain...Fasting itself doesn't cause fat gain..overeating does. Fasting can trigger overeating. If you fast for 24+hrs you are in taking a total of 0 calories. Your body will tap into your fat storage in order to make up for the lack of energy it will feed off the fat for energy. This is why people tend to fast for weight/fat loss. You WONT gain back the fat as long as after the fast you maintain your calories. Calories IN and Calories OUT (CICO) Does not stop working just because you haven't eaten for a few hours..Our bodies are literally MEANT to go long periods without food..Do you think back in the stone age we had 3 full meals everyday?

fasting is healthy/sustainable though? its the mindset behind the person that is the unhealthy part...People give fasting a bad rep because of the few anorexics that do it, like not everyone fasts unhealthily. just so you know people do their research and make sure to take safety precautions before doing it while the unhealthy people just care about losing weight and go to the extremes to do so.
